subject: Private deploy: DNS signer safelist + egress TLS fallback plan
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Singh <tara@acme-analytics.com>, Acme Sec Team <security-acct@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Private deploy: DNS signer safelist + egress TLS fallback plan

Hi Tara / Acme sec team,

Following our onboarding call, I wanted to capture a lightweight ops proposal for two interdependent items we need to lock down before the VPC private runtime goes live in your account:

1) DNS "signer" safelist (egress and inbound allowlists) — the IP ranges and AWS security group / firewall rules your team will permit so our private endpoint (+ ACME/CSR traffic) can reach your private resolver/CA.
2) Egress TLS fallback behavior — how Redwood should behave if the private CA path fails (OCSP unreachable, cert rotation gap, or DNS split-horizon mismatch).

Attachments: network-diagram-v2.png (high-level flow), sample-csr.txt (CSR template we’ll request), dns-signer-safelist.csv (example IP ranges + cloud-provider tags).

Key constraints and asks:
- We recommend declaring an explicit safelist of /24 CIDR blocks or provider-managed tags rather than ad-hoc host lists; this keeps rules stable across autoscaling. Example in dns-signer-safelist.csv.
- For private CA issuance we rely on a short-lived cert model (default 24h validity, automated rotation). We will push certs via the private control-plane tunnel; your resolver must allow inbound ACME validation from the listed signer IP ranges.
- For fallback we propose an ordered policy:
  a) Try private CA cert (primary)
  b) If private CA path fails, attempt OCSP-responder retry (1s backoff, 3 attempts)
  c) If still failing and the customer explicitly allows, temporarily present a public-trusted cert (short TTL) to avoid outage — only if the endpoint FQDN is covered and your compliance team approves fail-open.
  d) Otherwise fail-closed and route requests to a documented read-only maintenance page.

Questions for Acme:
- Do you have an existing safelist format we should consume (CSV vs Terraform-managed security group list)?
- Can you confirm whether fail-open (public cert fallback) is acceptable for non-PHI traffic?

Proposed timeline: safelist + CSR handoff deadline: 2026-10-11; test window 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-14.

Thanks — I’ll sync with Kimberly and Marissa on audit/logging items once you confirm the safelist format.

Connor O'Brien
Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai
Attachments: [network-diagram-v2.png (image/png), sample-csr.txt (text/plain), dns-signer-safelist.csv (text/csv)]
From: Tara Singh <tara@acme-analytics.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Sec Team <security-acct@acme-analytics.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T17:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: DNS signer safelist + egress TLS fallback plan

Connor — thanks for the summary and the artifacts. A few clarifying items from our side: 

- We prefer a Terraform-managed security group list (we can export tags), not a static CSV. Can you consume a tag-based allowlist?
- Our policy team will not allow automatic fail-open for any endpoint that touches identity metadata or billing flows. For analytics only endpoints, we may allow fail-open with explicit expiration (max 4 hours) and elevated monitoring.
- We need OCSP stapling behavior documented: if you staple responses, we can relax some firewall requirements for outbound OCSP checks. Can you confirm whether the private runtime will staple OCSP?
- Audit: we will need a proof of issuance (CSR fingerprint + issued cert) stored in our audit bucket. Can you push those artifacts to our onboarding S3 bucket (details below)?

S3 bucket (onboarding): s3://acme-onboarding/evidence/redwood/

If you can update the playbook to accept Terraform tag input and confirm OCSP stapling, we can meet the 10/11 deadline.

— Tara
Senior Cloud Security Engineer, Acme Analytics

Subject: Re: Private deploy: DNS signer safelist + egress TLS fallback plan

Tara — great notes. Answers inline and an updated ops flow: 

- Terraform tags: yes, we can consume an allowlist expressed as provider tags (AWS: security-group:allowed-for-redwood, or GCP: networkTag). Please share the tag names and the account/IRSA role we should use to read the tag list; alternatively we can accept an exported list in JSON from your infra team.

- Fail-open policy: understood. We will gate public-cert fallback behind an explicit flag per FQDN that your security team sets; default is fail-closed. If you set the flag we will: (1) reduce fallback window to 1 hour (configurable up to 4 hours per your comment), (2) generate alert to both teams and create an automatic incident ticket in INFRA-2234.

- OCSP stapling: Redwood runtime will staple OCSP responses for public-trusted certs when available. For private CA flows we support OCSP responders but do not staple by default unless you request it in the onboarding form. If you want stapling enabled for the private CA, we’ll need the OCSP responder endpoint and accept a single IP range for outgoing OCSP queries (this can be included in the Terraform tags).

- Audit artifacts: we can push CSR fingerprint + issued cert PEM to your onboarding S3 path; need an IAM role ARN for cross-account upload or a pre-signed upload step. We will also log issuance events to our control-plane audit topic (customer-visible) with a copy retained in our internal audit store for 90 days.

Next steps / action items I propose: 
- Acme infra: provide Terraform tag name(s) and either cross-account role ARN or allowlist JSON by 2026-10-08.
- Acme sec: declare fail-open permission per FQDN (list) by 2026-10-09.
- Redwood: enable OCSP stapling for private CA on request and prepare cross-account upload script by 2026-10-10.

I’ve uploaded a short HLD to Confluence (link in metadata) that maps the traffic flows and tag-to-rule translation.

Connor
Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: [dns-signer-safelist.csv]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-04T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: DNS signer safelist + egress TLS fallback plan

Connor / Tara — quick operational constraints from infra-sre side: 

- Audit and KMS: If we are pushing cert material cross-account, we need an S3 lifecycle policy and a short retention for CSR fingerprints (90 days) plus a documented KMS key for encrypting the uploads. We should capture the KMS key id in the onboarding form.
- Fail-open decision: leaning toward fail-closed by default. If Acme sets a fallback flag, we require a signed exception (email OK) and a short justification to keep a clean audit trail.
- Test plan: we will run two negative tests during the test window: (1) simulate OCSP responder downtime, (2) simulate DNS split mismatch where private resolver returns NX. Both tests will verify correct routing to maintenance or public fallback per the flag.

I filed INFRA-2234 with the test checklist and added you all as watchers. Please add any test endpoints in the Jira ticket.

Marissa Cole
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Acknowledged — a couple of final notes from product/security review: 

- SNI mapping: please include a small mapping table so we can validate SNI -> tenant during the rollout (helps detect accidental host collisions if Acme later re-uses an internal FQDN).
- Monitoring: add a metric for "private_cert_issuance_latency" and an alert when issuance latency > 20s for 3 consecutive checks. This is how we will detect degraded ACME/CA paths before failover kicks in.
- Compliance: we will not store private key material outside of the customer-managed KMS; only CSR fingerprints and issued cert PEMs are allowed in the audit bucket.

I’ll mark INFRA-2234 ready for test once the Acme infra team posts the tags/role.

Kimberly Park
Director, Product Security, Redwood Inference
